layers.title: Skeleton survey, 12 inches to the mile
layers.note: Roads, watercourses and bench marks only, surveyed for the Metropolitan Commission of Sewers before the railways and factories. Identification and date provisional.

layers.label: c.1862–75
layers.title: Five feet to the mile, first edition
layers.note: The most detailed early survey. Coverage is partial: sheets east of Stratford and around the docks are missing from the scanned set. Around Abbey Mills the sewer is drawn but the pumping station is not yet built.

layers.title: Six-inch, first edition
layers.note: County sheets for Essex, Middlesex and Kent joined at the Lea and the Thames. West Ham Abbey print works, chemical and tar works appear; much of the marsh is still open.

layers.title: Six-inch, second edition
layers.note: A seamless mosaic; individual sheets carry different revision dates within the range.

layers.title: Five feet to the mile, revision of 1891–95
layers.note: The book's central decade at the largest scale: every house, yard and gasholder. The same series gives the panorama its ground plan.

layers.label: 1890s–1910s
layers.title: 25-inch, London sheets
layers.note: Later revisions of the 1:2,500 series. A gap over Poplar, Bow Creek, Canning Town and Silvertown is real: those sheets are not in the scanned set, so use the five-foot plan there.

layers.title: One-inch, Revised New Series, coloured
layers.note: The regional view: West Ham within the industrial fringe of London.

layers.title: Bartholomew half-inch
layers.note: A commercial map with layer colouring for height; the low marshland reads clearly.

layers.title: One-inch, Popular Edition
layers.note: Just after the book's period; the bookend for comparison.

vectors.title: Industrial sites, 1865–75
vectors.credit: Jim Clifford with Steven Langlois and Anne Riitta Janhunen

places.title: Abbey Mills and the Channelsea
places.text: The sewer crossing where the panorama stands. Compare the empty marsh of 1848 with the works of 1893.

places.title: Stratford
places.text: Broadway, the station and the railway works that made Stratford an industrial town.

places.title: Three Mills
places.text: Tide mills on the Lea, older than any factory here.

places.title: Canning Town
places.text: Housing built on the marsh below high-water mark, beside the works it served.

places.title: Silvertown
places.text: Sugar, rubber, chemicals and the open drain in Wilton Street.

places.title: The Royal Docks
places.text: Victoria Dock of 1855 and the Royal Albert of 1880, cut through the Plaistow marshes.
